name: Margin Dollars with Volume
description: Calculate total gross margin dollars generated across a given sales volume.
business_contexts: a retailer totaling margin dollars across units sold in a period
a manufacturer totaling margin dollars across a production run
a distributor totaling margin dollars across a shipment
a subscription box company totaling margin dollars across a cohort
a wholesaler totaling margin dollars across an order
question_patterns: Given the price, cost, and volume below, what is the total gross margin in dollars?
Calculate the total margin dollars generated across the volume shown.
What is the total gross margin, in dollars, across the units given below?
Calculate the total dollar margin from the price, cost, and volume shown.
Using the figures given, what is the total margin earned across the full volume?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate per-unit margin = price − cost
Step 2: Calculate total margin dollars = per-unit margin × volume
key_insight: Margin dollars scale with volume, but margin percentage doesn't — a high-margin-percentage product sold in small volume can generate fewer total dollars than a thinner-margin product sold at scale.
common_mistakes: Reporting the per-unit margin instead of multiplying through by volume
Multiplying price (not the price-cost gap) by volume
framework_soundbite: Per-unit margin times volume — the two numbers only mean something once multiplied together.
display_context: Core Arithmetic • Margin Dollars with Volume
